statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): go-jose passes RSA modulus and prime values from a JWK to crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate without bounding them, and on Go 1.24 and later crafted values make that validation take cubic CPU time, so parsing an untrusted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. The advisory covers github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 before 4.1.6 and github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 up to 3.0.5, the latest v3 release: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q. The v4 fix is commit a0111f8, which bounds the RSA modulus, checks p * q = n and rejects private key material in JWS and JWE header keys; the v4.1.6 tag points at it: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. A backport to the v3 branch, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/0e502b87c7aa651155b11ae8e195ec33ce10230a, is not in any v3 release, so v3.0.5 is unfixed. We checked every published caddy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 23 builds, 2.11.4-r0 to the current 2.11.9-r5, on x86_64 and aarch64 (46 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/caddy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information shows the same go-jose modules on both architectures in every build: go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 in 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.4-r10, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 in 2.11.7-r0 to 2.11.7-r3, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.6 in 2.11.7-r4 to 2.11.9-r1, and go-jose/v4 v4.1.9 alone in 2.11.9-r2 to 2.11.9-r5; no replace directive applies to either module, and they are the only modules in the build information whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. The Go function table (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control) contains (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey from go-jose/v3 in every build up to 2.11.9-r1, so the unfixed v3 parsing code is linked there even in the builds whose go-jose/v4 is already fixed. From 2.11.9-r2 the function table holds no go-jose/v3 functions and a byte search of the program finds no go-jose/v3/json, go-jose/v3/cipher or go-jose/v3 JSONWebKey names; its (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are the go-jose/v4 ones, from v4.1.9 by the build information. As a fix-marker check we unpacked the x86_64 caddy-dev packages 2.11.9-r1 and 2.11.9-r2: both carry the error strings the go-jose/v4 fix adds ("invalid RSA private key, p * q != n" and "JWK contains private parameters"), 2.11.9-r1 still contains go-jose/v3 package-qualified names, and 2.11.9-r2 contains none. The Alpine 3.23 and 3.24 indexes list the same checksum for every build, so these are the same files in both. In v4.1.9 an oversized modulus returns ErrUnsupportedKeyType instead of the earlier "modulus too large" message. The range ends at 2.11.9-r2, the first build with neither an affected go-jose/v4 nor go-jose/v3.

The v4 fix is commit a0111f8, which bounds the RSA modulus, checks p * q = n and rejects private key material in JWS and JWE header keys; the v4.1.6 tag points at it: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. A backport to the v3 branch, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/0e502b87c7aa651155b11ae8e195ec33ce10230a, is not in any v3 release, so v3.0.5 is unfixed. We checked every published caddy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 23 builds, 2.11.4-r0 to the current 2.11.9-r5, on x86_64 and aarch64 (46 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/caddy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information shows the same go-jose modules on both architectures in every build: go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 in 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.4-r10, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 in 2.11.7-r0 to 2.11.7-r3, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.6 in 2.11.7-r4 to 2.11.9-r1, and go-jose/v4 v4.1.9 alone in 2.11.9-r2 to 2.11.9-r5; no replace directive applies to either module, and they are the only modules in the build information whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. The Go function table (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control) contains (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey from go-jose/v3 in every build up to 2.11.9-r1, so the unfixed v3 parsing code is linked there even in the builds whose go-jose/v4 is already fixed. The Alpine 3.23 and 3.24 indexes list the same checksum for every build, so these are the same files in both. In v4.1.9 an oversized modulus returns ErrUnsupportedKeyType instead of the earlier "modulus too large" message. The range ends at 2.11.9-r2, the first build with neither an affected go-jose/v4 nor go-jose/v3.

A backport to the v3 branch, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/0e502b87c7aa651155b11ae8e195ec33ce10230a, is not in any v3 release, so v3.0.5 is unfixed. We checked every published caddy-fips-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine security repository, which requires authentication: 23 builds, 2.11.4-r0 to the current 2.11.9-r5, on x86_64 and aarch64 (46 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/caddy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information shows the same go-jose modules on both architectures in every build: go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 in 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.4-r10, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 in 2.11.7-r0 to 2.11.7-r3, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.6 in 2.11.7-r4 to 2.11.9-r1, and go-jose/v4 v4.1.9 alone in 2.11.9-r2 to 2.11.9-r5; no replace directive applies to either module, and they are the only modules in the build information whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. The Go function table (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control) contains (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey from go-jose/v3 in every build up to 2.11.9-r1, so the unfixed v3 parsing code is linked there even in the builds whose go-jose/v4 is already fixed. From 2.11.9-r2 the function table holds no go-jose/v3 functions and a byte search of the program finds no go-jose/v3/json, go-jose/v3/cipher or go-jose/v3 JSONWebKey names; its (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are the go-jose/v4 ones, from v4.1.9 by the build information. As a fix-marker check we unpacked the x86_64 caddy-fips-dev packages 2.11.9-r1 and 2.11.9-r2: both carry the error strings the go-jose/v4 fix adds ("invalid RSA private key, p * q != n" and "JWK contains private parameters"), 2.11.9-r1 still contains go-jose/v3 package-qualified names, and 2.11.9-r2 contains none. The Alpine 3.23 and 3.24 indexes list the same checksum for every build, so these are the same files in both. In v4.1.9 an oversized modulus returns ErrUnsupportedKeyType instead of the earlier "modulus too large" message. The range ends at 2.11.9-r2, the first build with neither an affected go-jose/v4 nor go-jose/v3.

This owner covers the packages built from the Alpine docker recipe: docker, docker-engine, docker-cli and their support subpackages. Unpacked every subpackage of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository, 32 versions from 29.5.2-r0 to 29.10.0-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64 (29.10.0-r1 is so far published only as docker, docker-cli and docker-engine), and read the Go build information and the Go function names (from each program's function table; dockerd, docker-proxy and docker carry no ELF symbol table before 29.10.0-r1) of every ELF file. The only ELF files are three Go programs: /usr/bin/dockerd and /usr/bin/docker-proxy in docker-engine, and /usr/bin/docker in docker-cli. The other subpackages contain no ELF files. /usr/bin/docker is built from the docker/cli vendor tree and records no module versions in its build information up to 29.10.0-r0; in 29.10.0-r1 it lists them. go-jose is only in /usr/bin/docker: dockerd and docker-proxy contain no go-jose code or strings in any build. /usr/bin/docker links go-jose v4 in every build. Builds 29.5.2-r0 to 29.9.2-r3 package docker/cli v29.5.2 to v29.9.2, which vendor go-jose v4.1.4 or v4.1.5, and their /usr/bin/docker lacks the fix's "invalid RSA key, modulus too large" check. Builds 29.9.3-r0 to 29.10.0-r1 package v29.9.3 and v29.10.0, which vendor v4.1.7 (29.10.0-r1 lists go-jose v4.1.7 in its build information), and their /usr/bin/docker contains it (https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/v29.9.2/vendor/modules.txt, https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/v29.9.3/vendor/modules.txt). The first build with the fix is 29.9.3-r0. The advisory also lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 up to v3.0.5, with no fixed release; no build contains it: the docker/cli vendor trees for v29.5.2 to v29.10.0 list only go-jose v4 (v4.1.4, v4.1.5 or v4.1.7), and dockerd and docker-proxy list no go-jose module and contain no go-jose code or strings.

The v4 fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230 (tagged v4.1.6), bounds the RSA modulus and checks p * q = n in jwk.go, rejects private key material in the jwk and epk header parameters (jwk.go and shared.go), moves header sanitizing after the algorithm checks in jws.go and jwe.go, and in jws.go sets each signature's unprotected header before the headers are merged; its other changes are tests, error-message wrapping and moving the unused getJWK helper into test code. We checked every published envoy-gateway-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository: 67 builds, 1.7.5-r0 to the current 1.10.0-r2, on x86_64 and aarch64 (134 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/envoy-gateway, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replace directive, the same version on both architectures in every build: 1.7.5-r0 to 1.7.5-r16: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.7.5-r17 to 1.7.5-r20: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 1.8.2-r0 to 1.8.4-r5: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.8.5-r0 to 1.8.6-r0: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 1.8.6-r1 to 1.8.6-r4: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 1.9.0-r0 to 1.9.2-r4: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.9.3-r0: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 1.9.3-r1 to 1.10.0-r2: go-jose/v4 4.1.6. It lists no go-jose/v3 and no other module whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. Its Go function table (runtime.main found in every build as a control) contains go-jose v4's (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, the JWK parsing code the fix changes, in every build, so the module version decides. (*JSONWebKey).unmarshalJSON, a function the fix adds, is in the function table of every build with v4.1.6 and of no other build. As a byte check we unpacked the x86_64 envoy-gateway packages for Alpine 3.23 at 1.7.5-r16 and 1.7.5-r17, 1.8.6-r0 and 1.8.6-r1, and 1.9.3-r0 and 1.9.3-r1: the error strings the fix adds ("invalid RSA key, modulus too large" and "JWK contains private parameters") are absent from the first build of each pair and present in the second. The release lines are fixed at different points, so the range has 3 spans: the builds from 1.7.5-r0 to 1.7.5-r16 carry an affected go-jose, and 1.7.5-r17 is the first build after them with the fixed module; the builds from 1.8.2-r0 to 1.8.6-r0 carry an affected go-jose, and 1.8.6-r1 is the first build after them with the fixed module; the builds from 1.9.0-r0 to 1.9.3-r0 carry an affected go-jose, and 1.9.3-r1 is the first build after them with the fixed module. A second and third span are needed because the fixed builds of one release line sort below the unfixed early builds of the next line (1.7.5-r17 sorts below 1.8.2-r0, 1.8.6-r1 sorts below 1.9.0-r0). Every build from 1.9.3-r1 on, up to the current 1.10.0-r2, carries the fixed module.

Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replace directive, the same version on both architectures in every build: 1.7.5-r0 to 1.7.5-r16: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.7.5-r17 to 1.7.5-r20: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 1.8.2-r0 to 1.8.4-r5: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.8.5-r0 to 1.8.6-r0: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 1.8.6-r1 to 1.8.6-r4: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 1.9.0-r0 to 1.9.2-r4: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.9.3-r0: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 1.9.3-r1 to 1.10.0-r2: go-jose/v4 4.1.6. It lists no go-jose/v3 and no other module whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. Its Go function table (runtime.main found in every build as a control) contains go-jose v4's (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, the JWK parsing code the fix changes, in every build, so the module version decides. Its Go build information shows the same go-jose modules on both architectures in every build: go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 in 7.15.3-r0 to 7.15.4-r3, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 in 7.15.5-r0 to 7.15.5-r3, go-jose/v4 v4.1.6 alone in 7.15.5-r4, and go-jose/v4 v4.1.8 alone in 7.15.6-r0 to 7.15.6-r2; no replace directive applies to either module. The Go function table (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control) contains both (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey from go-jose/v3 and from go-jose/v4, and crypto/rsa.(*PrivateKey).Validate, in every build up to 7.15.5-r3, so the unbounded parsing code is linked there. statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): github.com/go-jose/go-jose passed the RSA modulus and primes of a JWK to crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate without bounds, and on Go 1.24 and later crafted values make that validation take cubic CPU time, so parsing an untrusted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. The advisory lists go-jose v4 up to 4.1.5 and go-jose v3 up to 3.0.5; it is fixed in v4.1.6. The fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230 (tagged v4.1.6), bounds the RSA modulus and checks p * q = n in jwk.go, rejects private key material in the jwk and epk header parameters (jwk.go and shared.go), moves header sanitizing after the algorithm checks in jws.go and jwe.go, and in jws.go sets each signature's unprotected header before the headers are merged; its other changes are tests, error-message wrapping and moving the unused getJWK helper into test code. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q. We read every published restic-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine package repository, 19 versions from 0.19.1-r0 to 0.20.0-r0 on x86_64 and aarch64, 38 packages, each matching its repository index checksum. Each holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/restic, built with CGO_ENABLED=0; we read its Go build information and its Go function table (pclntab), which is present in every build (runtime.main is found in each). Go module versions by build: 0.19.1-r0 to 0.19.1-r11: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 0.19.1-r12 to 0.20.0-r0: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; no build contains go-jose/v3. Every build links go-jose/v4's JWK parsing code ((*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are in the function table, attributed to the go-jose/v4 version in the build information). 0.19.1-r12 is the first build with go-jose/v4 4.1.6, from a DHI dependency update; the program in 0.19.1-r12 contains the error text the fix adds ("invalid RSA key, modulus too large") and the program in 0.19.1-r11 does not, on both architectures. Every earlier build carries go-jose/v4 4.1.4.

Each holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/restic, built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the Go FIPS 140-3 module (GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c); we read its Go build information and its Go function table (pclntab), which is present in every build (runtime.main is found in each). Go module versions by build: 0.19.1-r0 to 0.19.1-r11: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 0.19.1-r12 to 0.20.0-r0: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; no build contains go-jose/v3. Every build links go-jose/v4's JWK parsing code ((*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are in the function table, attributed to the go-jose/v4 version in the build information). 0.19.1-r12 is the first build with go-jose/v4 4.1.6, from a DHI dependency update; the program in 0.19.1-r12 contains the error text the fix adds ("invalid RSA key, modulus too large") and the program in 0.19.1-r11 does not, on both architectures. Every earlier build carries go-jose/v4 4.1.4.

CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): github.com/go-jose/go-jose does not bound the RSA modulus and primes in a JSON Web Key before passing them to crypto/rsa's PrivateKey.Validate, which on Go 1.24 and later takes time cubic in their size, so parsing a crafted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. go-jose v4 is fixed in 4.1.6 by commit a0111f8, which limits the RSA modulus size (returning "invalid RSA key, modulus too large"), checks that p * q = n and rejects private key material in JWS and JWE header keys; the v4.1.6 tag points at that commit. The advisory also lists go-jose v3 up to 3.0.5, with no fixed release. Sources: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. We checked every published scout-cli-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 24 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (48 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a Go program with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replacement, in every build, the same version on both architectures: v4.1.4 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r7, v4.1.5 in 1.23.1-r8 to 1.26.0-r2, v4.1.6 in 1.26.0-r3, and v4.1.9 in 1.26.0-r4 to 1.30.0-r0. It lists no other go-jose module (no go-jose v3, gopkg.in/square/go-jose or gopkg.in/go-jose); it also lists github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v3, github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 in every build, separate JOSE and JWT libraries that this advisory does not cover. Its Go function table contains go-jose v4's (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, the JWK parsing code the fix changes, in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control), so the module version decides. (*JSONWebKey).unmarshalJSON, a function the fix adds so that header parsing can reject keys with private parameters, is absent from every build up to 1.26.0-r2 and present in every build from 1.26.0-r3, and in every build the function table attributes the go-jose functions to source files of the version the build information lists. The range ends at 1.26.0-r3, the first build with the fixed module.

We read the Go build information (go version -m) and the function symbol table (go tool nm) of /usr/bin/trivy in each of the 38 published trivy-dev builds for Alpine 3.23, 0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12, on both x86_64 and aarch64. Each build installs one statically linked Go program, /usr/bin/trivy. CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): github.com/go-jose/go-jose passed the RSA modulus and primes of a JWK to crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate without bounds, and on Go 1.24 and later crafted values make that validation take cubic CPU time, so parsing an untrusted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. The advisory lists go-jose v4 up to 4.1.5 and go-jose v3 up to 3.0.5; it is fixed in v4.1.6. The fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230 (tagged v4.1.6), bounds the RSA modulus and checks p * q = n in jwk.go, rejects private key material in the jwk and epk header parameters (jwk.go and shared.go), moves header sanitizing after the algorithm checks in jws.go and jwe.go, and in jws.go sets each signature's unprotected header before the headers are merged; its other changes are tests, error-message wrapping and moving the unused getJWK helper into test code. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q. We read every published velero-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine package repository, 17 versions from 1.18.2-r1 to 1.18.4-r9 on x86_64 and aarch64, 34 packages, each matching its repository index checksum. Each holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/velero, built with CGO_ENABLED=0; we read its Go build information and its Go function table (pclntab), which is present in every build (runtime.main is found in each). Go module versions by build: 1.18.2-r1 to 1.18.4-r3: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.18.4-r4 to 1.18.4-r9: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; no build contains go-jose/v3. Every build links go-jose/v4's JWK parsing code ((*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are in the function table, attributed to the go-jose/v4 version in the build information). 1.18.4-r4 is the first build with go-jose/v4 4.1.6, from a DHI dependency update; the program in 1.18.4-r4 contains the error text the fix adds ("invalid RSA key, modulus too large") and the program in 1.18.4-r3 does not, on both architectures. Every earlier build carries go-jose/v4 4.1.4.

Read the Go build information of /usr/bin/alloy, the package's only program, in every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 (1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, amd64 and arm64; 43 versions on amd64 and 44 on arm64, where 1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only): every build before 1.21.3-0 is built with go-jose/v4 4.1.4 or 4.1.5, inside the affected range; 1.21.3-0 and every later build are built with go-jose/v4 4.1.6, which carry the fix. /usr/bin/alloy contains the go-jose/v4 JWK RSA parsing code that the fix changes (rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, rawJSONWebKey.rsaPublicKey and JSONWebKey.UnmarshalJSON) in every build, checked against the function names the Go linker records in each binary; the error message the fix adds ("invalid RSA key, modulus too large") is present in the binary from 1.21.3-0 onward and absent from every earlier build.

The advisory covers github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 before 4.1.6 and github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 up to 3.0.5, the latest v3 release: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q. The v4 fix is commit a0111f8, which bounds the RSA modulus, checks p * q = n and rejects private key material in JWS and JWE header keys; the v4.1.6 tag points at it: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. A backport to the v3 branch, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/0e502b87c7aa651155b11ae8e195ec33ce10230a, is not in any v3 release, so v3.0.5 is unfixed. We checked every published caddy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 23 builds, 2.11.4-0 to the current 2.11.9-5, on amd64 and arm64 (46 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/caddy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information shows the same go-jose modules on both architectures in every build: go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 in 2.11.4-0 to 2.11.4-10, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 in 2.11.7-0 to 2.11.7-3, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.6 in 2.11.7-4 to 2.11.9-1, and go-jose/v4 v4.1.9 alone in 2.11.9-2 to 2.11.9-5; no replace directive applies to either module, and they are the only modules in the build information whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. The Go function table (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control) contains (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey from go-jose/v3 in every build up to 2.11.9-1, so the unfixed v3 parsing code is linked there even in the builds whose go-jose/v4 is already fixed. From 2.11.9-2 the function table holds no go-jose/v3 functions and a byte search of the program finds no go-jose/v3/json, go-jose/v3/cipher or go-jose/v3 JSONWebKey names; its (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are the go-jose/v4 ones, from v4.1.9 by the build information. As a fix-marker check we unpacked the amd64 caddy-dev packages 2.11.9-1 and 2.11.9-2: both carry the error strings the go-jose/v4 fix adds ("invalid RSA private key, p * q != n" and "JWK contains private parameters"), 2.11.9-1 still contains go-jose/v3 package-qualified names, and 2.11.9-2 contains none. In v4.1.9 an oversized modulus returns ErrUnsupportedKeyType instead of the earlier "modulus too large" message. The range ends at 2.11.9-2, the first build with neither an affected go-jose/v4 nor go-jose/v3.

Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/envoy-gateway, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replace directive, the same version on both architectures in every build: 1.7.5-0 to 1.7.5-16: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.7.5-17 to 1.7.5-20: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 1.8.2-0 to 1.8.4-5: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.8.5-0 to 1.8.6-0: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 1.8.6-1 to 1.8.6-4: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 1.9.0-0 to 1.9.2-4: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.9.3-0: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 1.9.3-1 to 1.10.0-2: go-jose/v4 4.1.6. It lists no go-jose/v3 and no other module whose path names JOSE, JWT or JWX. CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): github.com/go-jose/go-jose does not bound the RSA modulus and primes in a JSON Web Key before passing them to crypto/rsa's PrivateKey.Validate, which on Go 1.24 and later takes time cubic in their size, so parsing a crafted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. go-jose v4 is fixed in 4.1.6 by commit a0111f8, which limits the RSA modulus size (returning "invalid RSA key, modulus too large"), checks that p * q = n and rejects private key material in JWS and JWE header keys; the v4.1.6 tag points at that commit. The advisory also lists go-jose v3 up to 3.0.5, with no fixed release. Sources: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. We checked every published scout-cli-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 24 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (48 packages), each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a Go program with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replacement, in every build, the same version on both architectures: v4.1.4 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-7, v4.1.5 in 1.23.1-8 to 1.26.0-2, v4.1.6 in 1.26.0-3, and v4.1.9 in 1.26.0-4 to 1.30.0-0. It lists no other go-jose module (no go-jose v3, gopkg.in/square/go-jose or gopkg.in/go-jose); it also lists github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v3, github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 in every build, separate JOSE and JWT libraries that this advisory does not cover. Its Go function table contains go-jose v4's (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, the JWK parsing code the fix changes, in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control), so the module version decides. (*JSONWebKey).unmarshalJSON, a function the fix adds so that header parsing can reject keys with private parameters, is absent from every build up to 1.26.0-2 and present in every build from 1.26.0-3, and in every build the function table attributes the go-jose functions to source files of the version the build information lists. The range ends at 1.26.0-3, the first build with the fixed module.

Sources: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. We checked every published scout-cli-fips package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian security repository, which requires authentication: 24 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (48 packages), each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a Go program with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replacement, in every build, the same version on both architectures: v4.1.4 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-7, v4.1.5 in 1.23.1-8 to 1.26.0-2, v4.1.6 in 1.26.0-3, and v4.1.9 in 1.26.0-4 to 1.30.0-0. It lists no other go-jose module (no go-jose v3, gopkg.in/square/go-jose or gopkg.in/go-jose); it also lists github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v3, github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 in every build, separate JOSE and JWT libraries that this advisory does not cover. Its Go function table contains go-jose v4's (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, the JWK parsing code the fix changes, in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control), so the module version decides. (*JSONWebKey).unmarshalJSON, a function the fix adds so that header parsing can reject keys with private parameters, is absent from every build up to 1.26.0-2 and present in every build from 1.26.0-3, and in every build the function table attributes the go-jose functions to source files of the version the build information lists. The range ends at 1.26.0-3, the first build with the fixed module.

Sources: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. We checked every published scout-sbom-indexer-oci-config package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages), each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds a single file, /opt/docker/config/scout-sbom-indexer.yaml, a YAML configuration file for the image; it contains no program, library or Go code. Debian has fixed this CVE in unstable but not in Debian 13 (trixie), where its golang-github-go-jose-go-jose package is marked no-dsa; this decision rests on what this package contains, not on that status. go-jose is not part of this package; the sbom-indexer program ships in the scout-sbom-indexer and scout-sbom-indexer-dev packages, which are assessed separately.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): github.com/go-jose/go-jose does not bound the RSA modulus and primes in a JSON Web Key before passing them to crypto/rsa's PrivateKey.Validate, which on Go 1.24 and later takes time cubic in their size, so parsing a crafted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. go-jose v4 is fixed in 4.1.6 by commit a0111f8, which limits the RSA modulus size (returning "invalid RSA key, modulus too large"), checks that p * q = n and rejects private key material in JWS and JWE header keys; the v4.1.6 tag points at that commit. The advisory also lists go-jose v3 up to 3.0.5, with no fixed release. Sources: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6. We checked every published scout-sbom-indexer package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages), each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a Go program with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information lists github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4, with no replacement, in every build, the same version on both architectures: v4.1.4 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-6, v4.1.5 in 1.23.1-8 to 1.26.0-1, v4.1.6 in 1.26.0-2 to 1.29.0-0, and v4.1.9 in 1.29.0-1 to 1.30.0-0. It lists no other go-jose module (no go-jose v3, gopkg.in/square/go-jose or gopkg.in/go-jose); it also lists github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v3, github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 in every build, separate JOSE and JWT libraries that this advisory does not cover. Its Go function table contains go-jose v4's (*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey, the JWK parsing code the fix changes, in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control), so the module version decides. (*JSONWebKey).unmarshalJSON, a function the fix adds so that header parsing can reject keys with private parameters, is absent from every build up to 1.26.0-1 and present in every build from 1.26.0-2, and in every build the function table attributes the go-jose functions to source files of the version the build information lists. The range ends at 1.26.0-2, the first build with the fixed module.

CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q): github.com/go-jose/go-jose passed the RSA modulus and primes of a JWK to crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate without bounds, and on Go 1.24 and later crafted values make that validation take cubic CPU time, so parsing an untrusted JWK, including one embedded in a JWS or JWE header, can exhaust CPU. The advisory lists go-jose v4 up to 4.1.5 and go-jose v3 up to 3.0.5; it is fixed in v4.1.6. The fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a0111f82742fa92bceec9ede40845e73319e6230 (tagged v4.1.6), bounds the RSA modulus and checks p * q = n in jwk.go, rejects private key material in the jwk and epk header parameters (jwk.go and shared.go), moves header sanitizing after the algorithm checks in jws.go and jwe.go, and in jws.go sets each signature's unprotected header before the headers are merged; its other changes are tests, error-message wrapping and moving the unused getJWK helper into test code. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q. We read every published velero-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian package repository, 17 versions from 1.18.2-1 to 1.18.4-9 on amd64 and arm64, 34 packages, each matching its repository index checksum. Each holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/velero, built with CGO_ENABLED=0; we read its Go build information and its Go function table (pclntab), which is present in every build (runtime.main is found in each). Go module versions by build: 1.18.2-1 to 1.18.4-3: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 1.18.4-4 to 1.18.4-9: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; no build contains go-jose/v3. Every build links go-jose/v4's JWK parsing code ((*JSONWebKey).UnmarshalJSON and rawJSONWebKey.rsaPrivateKey are in the function table, attributed to the go-jose/v4 version in the build information). 1.18.4-4 is the first build with go-jose/v4 4.1.6, from a DHI dependency update; the program in 1.18.4-4 contains the error text the fix adds ("invalid RSA key, modulus too large") and the program in 1.18.4-3 does not, on both architectures. Every earlier build carries go-jose/v4 4.1.4.
